repo.description: A high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs
repo.name: vllm

detail.body:
## Overview This PR enables the recipe's two fp8 cache flags on the Qwen4Exp AMD (ROCm) QSA path, mirroring the NVIDIA-side support: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 ... \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config.indexer_kv_dtype fp8 ``` Three commits: 1. **`[ROCm][Bugfix] Apply FP8 cache scales to FNUZ destinations in the AMD fused QSA prepare`** — `_to_dst_dtype` divided by the main-attention KV cache scale only for `tl.float8e4nv` (OCP) destinations. On ROCm, FP8 KV caches type as `float8_e4m3fnuz` (Triton `tl.float8e4b8`), so the scale was never applied: FP8-typed destinations received `k_scale`/`v_scale` times the intended magnitude. Latent before this PR (the AMD path restricted KV dtypes to auto/bfloat16), required before FP8 KV can be enabled. 2. **`Support indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`** — wires `--attention-config.indexer_kv_dtype` through `amd/indexer_qsa.py`, mirroring the NVIDIA reference (`fp8` → `torch.float8_e4m3fn` for the compressed key cache and the query side; the raw state cache stays bf16). The fused kernel already handled fp8-typed indexer caches; only the wiring and test coverage were missing (the indexer cells were skipped as "bf16-only"). 3. **`Support fp8 main KV cache`** — lifts the remaining dtype gates and reinterprets the uint8 main cache at the boundaries in the platform's native fp8 flavor — **OCP (`float8_e4m3fn`) on gfx950/CDNA4, FNUZ (`float8_e4m3fnuz`) on gfx942/CDNA3** — matching the C++ cache-update op, which follows the platform flavor the same way (`HIP_FP8_TYPE_OCP`), so no C++ changes are needed. The sparse attention kernel gains an `IS_FP8` constexpr with the NVIDIA port's casts (fp8 K upcast to the query dtype for the QK dot; fp8 V to fp16 for the PV dot). A `kv_reads_bypass_flash_attn` class attribute lets the QSA impl skip the FlashAttention library's kv-dtype support check, since QSA reads its cache through its own Triton kernel. The test's `main_fp8` parametrization covers both flavors. ## Claims - **KV capacity: +33%** at TP1 (2,505,113 → 3,336,874 tokens) with both flags; the main KV cache is the dominant consumer and halves. - **Quality-neutral** on GSM8K 5-shot (6-run pairs): strict-match 0.899 vs 0.902 baseline; flexible-extract 0.881 vs 0.895 with fully overlapping run ranges. - **Quality-neutral** on GPQA-Diamond (198 questions, greedy): 0.4596 vs 0.4747 flexible-extract (within the ±3.5 pt binomial SE); NIAH retrieval identical (90/90 at every length and depth, 8K-32K). - **Greedy outputs byte-identical** on the arithmetic/coherence gates in-session (391 ×3 + a France continuation, temperature 0). - **Throughput**: decode is unchanged; concurrency-16 aggregate is ~6% lower with both flags (documented tradeoff below — the flags are opt-in, a capacity-vs-concurrency choice). ## Validation **Unit tests** (gfx950 / MI355X, ROCm 7.2.3, torch 2.13.0+rocm7.2): ```bash pytest -v tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py ``` `48 passed` at this PR's HEAD — the `main_fp8` parametrization now covers `bf16 | fnuz | ocp` crossed with the indexer dtype. Before commit 1, the fp8 cells failed with a systematic mis-scale (stored/expected code differences ~8 steps across the whole cache — exactly the 0.5 scale factor). Before commit 3, serving with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` failed at four dtype gates (impl, layer, backend init, and the FlashAttention base check). Raw captures:
Red run (commit 1's fix reverted), 8 FAILED — the mis-scale signature ``` FAILED tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py::test_qsa_fused_prepare_matches_unfused[mrope-indexer_dtype0-True] FAILED tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py::test_qsa_fused_prepare_matches_unfused[text-indexer_dtype0-True] FAILED tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_prepare_amd.py::test_qsa_fused_prepare_matches_unfused[mrope-model-1d-indexer_dtype0-True] ... (8 total) ============ 8 failed, 8 passed, 16 skipped, 14 warnings in 11.37s ============ ``` The assertion output shows the stored/expected code differences are a systematic ~8 code steps across the whole cache (the k_scale=0.5 mis-scale), far outside the tolerance (`code_diff <= 2 | abs_diff <= RTOL*|expected| + 2*ATOL`).
Pre-change boot failures with --kv-cache-dtype fp8 (the lifted gates) ``` NotImplementedError: Qwen4Exp QSA requires a BF16 main KV cache # impl + layer + backend gates NotImplementedError: FlashAttention does not support fp8 kv-cache on this device. # FA base check ```
Green at HEAD ``` ======================= 48 passed, 14 warnings in 16.10s ======================= ``` `pytest -q tests/models/qwen4_exp/ --ignore=tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_amd.py` → `186 passed, 86 skipped`; `pytest -q tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_qsa_amd.py` → `16 passed`. (Whole-directory collection has a pre-existing custom-op registration clash, reproducible on the clean tree.)
**Serving / capacity** (MI355X, TP1, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, max-model-len 16384, max-num-seqs 16, no MTP; identical flags otherwise): | config | GPU KV cache (tokens) | greedy gates | | --- | --- | --- | | bf16 baseline | 2,505,113 | 391 ×3, France continuation exact | | indexer fp8 | 2,541,158 (+1.5%) | identical | | main KV fp8 | 3,238,570 (+29.3%) | identical | | both | **3,336,874 (+33.2%)** | identical |
Raw boot-log lines ``` bf16: GPU KV cache size: 2,505,113 tokens indexer fp8: GPU KV cache size: 2,541,158 tokens main KV fp8: GPU KV cache size: 3,238,570 tokens both: GPU KV cache size: 3,336,874 tokens ```
At TP4 (cards 4-7, same protocol), the indexer-fp8 gain grows with tensor parallelism because the indexer side cache is replicated (`num_kv_heads=1`, unsharded) while the main KV shards: 11,541,981 → 11,893,691 tokens (**+3.05%**, vs +1.5% at TP1; the absolute gain scales ~9×). Note the FP8 checkpoint at TP4 currently needs `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0` and `--disable-custom-all-reduce` on this tree — both are the failure modes #60839 automates fallbacks for. **Quality: GSM8K 5-shot** (chat template, 250-problem deterministic subset, 6 runs per config, lm_eval against the served endpoint): | config | flexible-extract (6 runs) | mean | strict-match (6 runs) | mean | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | bf16 | 0.900 0.888 0.908 0.884 0.900 0.892 | 0.895 | 0.888 0.904 0.904 0.904 0.904 0.908 | 0.902 | | indexer fp8 | 0.900 0.892 0.876 0.892 0.884 0.896 | 0.890 | 0.908 0.896 0.884 0.916 0.884 0.912 | 0.900 | | both fp8 | 0.892 0.884 0.868 0.876 0.884 0.880 | 0.881 | 0.896 0.904 0.896 0.884 0.904 0.908 | 0.899 | Strict-match is neutral; flexible-extract is −1.4 points with fully overlapping ranges. All configs share the same build, so the comparison is internally controlled. *(Correction: our earlier caveat attributed the TP1 GSM8K absolutes to the un-merged #60816 — that was wrong. The relevant fix (#55104) is already in this build, and TP1 and TP2 score identically on it. The table's numbers are consistent with the shared lm_eval setup — same build, server config, and harness across all arms — so the claim is the within-build delta.)*
Raw score lines (first two runs per config) ``` bf16: |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.900|± |0.019| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.888|± |0.0200| both fp8:|gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.892|± |0.0197| |gsm8k| 3|flexible-extract| 5|exact_match|↑ |0.884|± |0.0203| ```
**Quality: GPQA-Diamond and NIAH long-context retrieval** (added per review; both arms on the PR head, TP1, MI355X, max-model-len 32768, greedy temperature 0): | arm | GPQA-Diamond, flexible-extract (198 q) | NIAH ({8, 16, 32}K × depths {0…100}% × 2 needles × 3 seeds) | | --- | --- | --- | | bf16 (auto) | 0.4596 ± 0.0355 | 90/90 = 100% | | fp8 main + indexer | 0.4747 ± 0.0356 | 90/90 = 100% | GPQA is within the binomial SE (fp8 nominally +1.5 points); NIAH retrieval is perfect in both arms at every (length, depth) cell — the fp8 indexer scores and fp8 main KV preserve long-context retrieval identically up to 32K. Strict-match is 0.00 in both arms (a CoT answer-format artifact of this task; flexible-extract is the paired metric). At this eval's max-model-len (32768), the same boots hold 3,336,874 → 5,005,312 KV tokens (+49.9%); the headline +33% above was measured at max-model-len 16384 — the capacity metric on current main depends on max-model-len through the concurrency formula, so capacity comparisons are same-len only.
Commands ``` lm_eval --model local-completions \ --model_args model=...,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=16,tokenizer_backend=huggingface,max_gen_toks=2048 \ --tasks gpqa_diamond_cot_zeroshot --seed 0 --apply_chat_template # NIAH: Paul Graham essay haystack, magic-number needle at depth d, # substring-scored; {8192, 16384, 32768} x {0, 25, 50, 75, 100}% x 2 # needles per run, 3 seeded runs per arm. ```
## The concurrency-16 tradeoff (and where the fix work is) Decode throughput is unchanged (110.5-110.6 vs 111.0-111.5 tok/s baseline, 7k context / 512 tokens). At concurrency 16, aggregate throughput is ~6% lower with both flags, stable across host load levels: | config | conc16 aggregate tok/s (×3) | | --- | --- | | bf16 baseline (same session) | 509.0 / 510.1 / 508.4 | | indexer fp8 | 509.1 / 512.1 / 510.6 | | main KV fp8 only | 491.7 / 510.3 / 497.9 | | both fp8 | 464-485 across 6 runs and two load levels | Both flags are opt-in, so this is a capacity-vs-concurrency choice for the operator: +33% KV capacity (more concurrent long-context requests) against ~6% at conc16 on this workload. Where we believe the fix work is: - The `IS_FP8` cast sites in the sparse attention kernel (`amd/ops/qsa.py`): fp8 K is upcast to the query dtype (bf16) before the QK dot and fp8 V to fp16 before the PV dot, per the NVIDIA port's measurements on its own hardware. On gfx950 the fp8 tensor cores are native, so **revisiting native fp8 QK dots on CDNA4** is the first thing to try — the NVIDIA-side comment's "fp8 QK measured slower and less accurate" does not necessarily transfer to this arch. - A concurrency-16 profile of the attention kernel to pin the mechanism (decode is unaffected, so the cost only appears under batch). ## Details - **Flavor design**: the C++ cache-update op selects its fp8 flavor from the platform (`HIP_FP8_TYPE_OCP`: FNUZ on CDNA3, OCP on CDNA4), and the cache is allocated as uint8. This PR reinterprets the cache at the typed boundaries in the same per-arch flavor, so the fused Triton writes, the triton reads, and the C++ unfused-path writes all agree on both arches with zero C++ changes. The `_to_dst_dtype` scale divide covers both flavors (commit 1). - **Cross-arch scope**: validated end-to-end on gfx950 (MI355X). The gfx942/FNUZ leg is design-consistent and kernel-side-unit-validated (the fnuz flavor cells pass), but a serve-level gfx942 run has not been performed; happy to add one on request. - **Known gap**: per-tensor dequant scales are not yet folded into the kernels. Default scales are 1.0 and this checkpoint declares no `kv_cache_scheme`, so it is a no-op today; the NVIDIA port's host-side folding (K scale into the softmax scale, V scale as the output scale) is the follow-up if calibrated scales ever matter. - TP4 notes: the FP8 checkpoint at TP4 on this tree requires `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE=0` and `--disable-custom-all-reduce` (#60839 automates both fallbacks); with those flags both TP4 arms serve and gate correctly. - ruff check + format clean on all touched files; DCO-signed commits.

You're right — the fold is missing. The NVIDIA port solves this by absorbing the scales into the attention math rather than doing an explicit multiply-back: `k_scale` is pre-multiplied into the softmax scale (`softmax_scale = head_dim^-0.5 * k_scale`) and `v_scale` becomes the kernel's output scale, folded into the reciprocal normalizer (with the split-K LSE kept unscaled so the merge stays correct — see `nvidia/ops/qsa.py`).

It's inert on this path today because all three mechanisms that could set non-unit scales are blocked: `set_default_quant_scales` hard-codes 1.0, the layer raises on `quant_config.kv_cache_scheme`, and `--calculate-kv-scales` doesn't participate in QSA. But the write-divide/read-no-multiply pairing is only sound under an invariant nothing enforces.

I've added a fail-fast in `forward_qsa` (87b62b06e8): `NotImplementedError` if fp8 KV and either scale != 1.0, with the message pointing at the NVIDIA fold as the fix. Happy to port the fold in a follow-up if you'd prefer that over the guard.

Unlike the main cache (flavor dictated by the C++ cache-update op, which follows the platform), the compressed indexer cache is a standalone typed tensor that never passes through C++, and its contents are scale-free e4m3 (Q and compressed K are RMSNormed before quantization). The NVIDIA reference also hardcodes `e4m3fn`. Review feedback addressed in cbe8d5eff6: flavor selection now goes through `current_platform.fp8_dtype()` everywhere (read-side views, write-side view, and the test's cache construction), and the test is back to `main_fp8=[False, True]` with the flavor taken from the platform at runtime.

For the Buildkite ask: `mirror:` supports a single AMD target per step, so MI300X coverage is a native `device: mi300_1` step — the same pattern as the lm_eval MI300 jobs — running the same AMD commands as the MI355 mirror. Those tests had no MI300 CI before, so the fnuz-flavor cells now get native gfx942 coverage.

Thanks @mjkvaak-amd — caveat corrected: the #55104 fix is in this build and our TP1/TP2 scores match on it; the table's numbers are consistent with the shared lm_eval setup (same build, config, and harness across all arms). One finding that may be useful for the tracker: GSM8K absolutes on this model proved very harness-sensitive in our measurement — lm_eval versions differ in their 5-shot example selection, worth ~20 points on identical serving — so cross-report comparisons probably need the eval invocation pinned.

Thanks for the review!

**GPQA and NIAH**: coming — I'll capture bf16 vs both-fp8 pairs and add the tables.

Implemented the same per-layer resolution as the standard Attention path in 87b62b06e8 (skipped layers resolve to auto/bf16 regardless of the global dtype, with an `info_once` log). The indexer cache follows `indexer_kv_dtype` independently, which is correct behavior (it's a separate cache, not the main KV).

All other feedback addressed in 87b62b06e8 — the k_scale guard, dtype consolidation, the ClassVar cleanup, and the comment removals. Details in the thread replies.

GPQA-Diamond and NIAH results are in the PR description now (both arms on the PR head, TP1, greedy):

- **NIAH** ({8, 16, 32}K haystacks × 5 insertion depths × 2 needles × 3 seeds): 90/90 = 100% in both arms — every (length, depth) cell identical, so the fp8 indexer scoring and fp8 main KV preserve long-context retrieval up to 32K.
